study.title: Predicting acupuncture efficacy for functional dyspepsia based on functional brain network features: a machine learning study
study.study_design: Prediction analysis based on data from two randomized controlled trials; machine learning study using pre-treatment functional brain network features
study.randomization: Participants were collected from two randomized controlled trials; the current prediction study itself does not describe additional randomization
study.population: Functional dyspepsia patients recruited at the campus and Hospital of Chengdu University of Traditional Chinese Medicine
study.inclusion_criteria: (i) met the Rome III diagnostic criteria for FD; (ii) were right-handed and aged from 18 to 40 years; (iii) were college degree or above; (iv) did not take part in any clinical trial in the past three months; (v) did not take any gastrointestinal prokinetic agent at least two weeks before enrolment
study.exclusion_criteria: (i) suffered from other organic or metabolic diseases; (ii) complicated with other functional gastrointestinal diseases such as irritable bowel syndrome; (iii) afflicted with migraine, fibromyalgia, dysmenorrhea, or other chronic pain disorders; (iv) accompanied with severe depression or anxiety; (v) had a history of head trauma, gastrointestinal surgery, psychiatric, or neurological disorders; (vi) had brain lesions or severe cerebrum anatomical asymmetry; (vii) had any contraindication of MRI scans such as implanted ferromagnetic metal and claustrophobia; (viii) were pregnant or lactating, or intended to pregnant in the 6 months

arms.dropouts: 11 FD patients were excluded at baseline because of excessive head motion; 72 of 89 finished the second MRI scanning; 7 patients were excluded for data recording error or excessive head movement, leaving 65 patients for longitudinal analysis

interventions.treatment_period_exact: four weeks (once per day for 5 days continuously each week, with 2 days intervals to the next week)

neuroimaging_methods.analysis_software_exact: LIBSVM toolbox at MATLAB 2017b; SPM12; DPARSF4.1
neuroimaging_methods.motion_exclusion_exact: translation > 2 mm or rotation > 2°; mean framewise displacement > 0.2; or a percentage of the framewise displacement exceeded 0.2 > 30%
primary_neuroimaging_metrics: functional brain network edges (rsFC between two ICs)
statistical_thresholds_exact: P < 0.05, false discovery rate (FDR) corrected (for within-group comparisons, between-group comparisons, and correlation analyses of predictive features)
P < 0.05, FDR corrected (feature filtering threshold for prediction model: α = 0.15 Spearman correlation)
permutation test: number of repetitions = 1000 (statistical efficiency = 0.001)

extraction_notes.note: Details of acupuncture prescriptions and manipulations are reported in Supplementary 1, which is not provided in the PDF. Needle type, size, depth, retention time, session duration, and specific manipulation technique cannot be extracted.
MRI scanning parameters (TR, TE, voxel size, scan duration, normalization template, smoothing, filtering) are reported in Supplementary 1, which is not provided.
Details of fMRI data preprocessing steps are in Supplementary 1, which is not provided.
Full list of 38 critical predictive features and their weights are in Supplementary 4. Only the top three features and IC relative weights are reported in the main text.
The 14 edges with baseline rsFC significantly correlated with SID improvements (P < 0.05, FDR corrected) are detailed in Supplementary 5. Only two are named in the main text (IC33-IC28, IC61-IC77).

Full details of within-group, between-group rsFC changes of predictive features are in Supplementary 6. Individual edges beyond those named in main text/figure cannot be extracted without the supplement.
Detailed information of the 35 selected ICs is in Supplementary 3. Full spatial and functional descriptions of all ICs are not in the main text.
The flow chart of acupuncture efficacy prediction analysis is in Supplementary 2, not provided.
Deqi/sensory responses to acupuncture are not reported or assessed in this study. The paper does not mention any sensory rating instruments or deqi scales.
Expectancy, credibility, and blinding success were not assessed or reported in this study.
Adverse events are not reported in this paper.
Coordinate space (MNI or Talairach) is not explicitly stated in the main text. No coordinate tables are present; results are reported at the network edge/IC level without MNI coordinates.
No sham acupuncture arm is included in this study. All patients received verum acupuncture. The paper discusses sham acupuncture for FD in limitations but does not include a sham arm.

The IC relative weights displayed in Fig. 2e show numerical values (1.12, 0.83, 0.67, 0.68, 0.48, and smaller values for other ICs). The exact values for all ICs beyond those labeled in the figure text cannot be verified from the PDF text alone. Values extracted for the top 5 ICs are based on reported text and figure bar values, which may have OCR imprecision for smaller bars.

The paper states 'the caudate (IC33), SOFC (IC15), hippocampus (IC61), anterior insula (IC28), and MOFC (IC43) in the CCN had the highest relative weights' but the anterior insula (IC28) is listed as part of CCN, which is an unusual assignment. This is the paper's own classification.

Table 1 has n=51 responders and n=38 non-responders (total 89 for prediction analysis). Table 2 has n=39 responders and n=26 non-responders (total 65 for longitudinal analysis). These are distinct subsamples and are kept separate in extraction.

The between-group comparison of rsFC changes showed P < 0.05 uncorrected but not significant after FDR correction. The correlation analyses of edge changes with SID improvements also showed P < 0.05 uncorrected but not significant after FDR. These results are retained with explicit annotation of correction status.

The paper states participants were collected from two RCTs, but the current study is a prediction analysis with no control arm or sham arm. The design is observational/prognostic. All patients received verum acupuncture.
The paper does not report PMID. DOI is reported on the article header.

IC relative weights for all ICs beyond the top ~5 are displayed in Fig. 2e as a bar chart. Precise numeric values for the smaller bars (e.g., IC7, IC37, IC62, IC79, IC1, IC23, IC49, IC36, IC54, IC27, IC45, IC8, IC58, IC3, IC56, IC67, IC55, IC50, IC71, IC69, IC21, IC80) cannot be precisely confirmed from main text alone. Some values appear in the figure label area.
